questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to challenge myself to live and study in a completely new environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did enjoy Japan as a destination but was wholly dissatisfied by the academic workload and challenge. For anyone going to Japan to study, beware that their standards are considerably lower and if your goal is to go there for an academic opportunity, you might be disappointed.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The orientation for international students and material provided beforehand was great and will help anyone who is anxious about the bureaucratic processes, as well as registration procedures. However, every graduate school at Waseda does things individually, so I cannot speak for the others.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Orientation meetings, e-mails, etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Finding housing was rather easy, even though it can be a time-consuming process. Be aware that any communication with Japanese realtors and rental companies might solely be in Japanese, so translation tools are your only guide. This also concerns contracts and documents you will have to sign regarding your room/apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: See my comments above.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration was available only a few weeks before the start of the semester - rather late. I was anxious about getting all the courses I had pre-approved, but this was not an issue in the end.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did not require any help for registration, but there would have been academic coordinators at the school to help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to successfully register for all classes I wanted/had pre-approved.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: See my comments above about the registration process starting rather late.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say that the academic level/standard in Japan is shockingly low. I confirmed this with other exchange students who were not in the social sciences and they agreed with this assessment. Be aware of this when considering Japan as a destination for a scholarly challenge.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are student-led discussions, but not to the level of KU. It largely depends on the professors, and I have found that Japanese professors prefer a lecture-type class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Europe and Asia; Comparative Regionalism; Citizenship, Culture, and Community; Political Economy of Development;

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are too many courses at Waseda compared to the few I took to be able to recommend a specific one.

What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There would have been regular events for international students at the University, but I did not partake in them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not partake in any non-academic activities at the school.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Japan has an incredible rail network and there is a lot to do in the greater Tokyo region, such as hiking, cultural activities, exploring other cities, etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Be aware that the level of English really low and oftentimes non-existent, even in a metropolis such as Tokyo. Communication is often difficult and Japanese is a rather difficult language to master even at a basic level. However, Japanese people are very understanding of this and will do their best to accommodate you.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: See my comments above about the Japanese language. I practiced Japanese for more than half a year and still found it very difficult to communicate, even at a basic level. However, it was rewarding to at least be able to read some of the signage, and this should not be a discouragement if you want to go to Japan.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Japanese culture is widely known for its high levels of politeness. Even if you can never really be sure if someone is polite to you because it is a social convention or because they are actually a nice person, it nevertheless makes things like the communicative barrier a bit easier.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be aware that the studying abroad can oftentimes be difficult, whether this be the distance from home, the academic challenge, cultural barriers, or other issues. However, I would strongly urge everyone to think about going on exchange, since this is an opportunity you will most likely never get again this easily in your life.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't think about it too much. If Tokyo - or Japan - is a destination of interest to you, then do it. Even if you are a bit disappointed in the end, it is a valuable experience in your life that no-one will be able to take from you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I was able to travel a lot around Japan and appreciate the different facets of its nature, culture, cuisine, etc.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The fact that academically, it was a major letdown.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
